text:
mia: FYI bringing up r3b-lite-v2 (int8) on staging, quick smoke showed NDCG +0.02, MRR -0.04. odd combo, filing here to triage

sam: hmm that divergence usually hints at tail/top1 shifting, maybe tiebreaker behavior changed after quant?

jess: did you keep candidate ordering identical to fp32 baseline? even small shuffle can drop MRR

mia: ordering preserved, same shortlist, same candidate text. eval harness ran with sampling seed=42, batch_size=256

omar: can you post the eval config and a minimal repro? also which dataset split (prod sample / goldset)?

mia: ran primarily on a 5k prod-sampled queries bucket + 1k goldset holdout. config: ```{
  "model": "r3b-lite-v2-int8",
  "batch_size": 256,
  "seed": 42,
  "candidate_pool": "prod_sample_5k",
  "metrics": ["ndcg@10","mrr@10"]
}```

jess: two quick checks: tokenizer parity (casing/whitespace) and float->int rounding nondet. Did you use our staged quant kernels or the fast path?

mia: using fast path hybrid kernels (kvpack enabled). tokenizer should be same but I'll re-run with explicit casefold step.

leo: CI bot ran a smoke earlier, flagged nondeterministic seed in the int8 runtime once: ci-bot: "warning: quant-runtime: seed_non_deterministic=true in /etc/quant/conf"

sam: that could explain MRR drop if tie resolution depends on nondet ordering. Set determinism flag and re-eval.

mia: re-run queued: will toggle `seed_non_deterministic=false` and rerun both prod sample and goldset. also will run fp32 baseline on same query ids to get per-query diffs.

omar: when you have per-query diffs, please dump top-5 difference examples to paste here. we should look for consistent pattern (short queries, punctuation, case).

jess: also consider stratified bootstrapping to get CIs. 5k is okay but tail behavior can be noisy; bootstrap 1000 samples of 1k each and check MRR distribution.

mia: ack. schedule: 1) set determinism flag, 2) fp32 vs int8 per-query diff, 3) tokenizer parity run, 4) bootstrap CIs. ETA ~2h.

sam: nice. if MRR still down after determinism + tokenizer, next suspect is quant-induced score compression. run score histograms (fp32 vs int8) to see tie density increase.

mia: good point. I'll dump histograms and a small script to compute tie counts at topk. snippet I'll use: ```python
# quick tie counter
def topk_ties(scores, k=10):
  tops = scores.argsort()[::-1][:k]
  return sum(1 for i in range(len(tops)-1) if abs(scores[tops[i]]-scores[tops[i+1]])<1e-6)
```

leo: tagging @ci-bot to ensure determinism flag rollout on staging infra once validated. ci-bot: "noted, will create infra task if you confirm"

omar: if we find score compression, also try temperature rescale or small learned bias per-candidate-type as a mitigation while we debug quant kernels.

mia: update: after determinism flag, preliminary rerun shows MRR gap narrowed to -0.01 on prod sample and -0.015 on goldset. NDCG still +0.015. dumping per-query top-5 diffs now (will paste few examples)

jess: promising. that pattern (ndcg up, mrr down) often means improvements in average ranking but slight worsening at rank1 — maybe int8 nudges some borderline docs into rank1 that displace highly-clicked ones.

mia: pasted two examples: query "reset password" -> fp32 top1 docs A, int8 top1 doc B (B is duplicate content from another doc id), query "api rate limit" -> fp32 top1 doc C, int8 top1 doc D (D has extra HTML).

sam: duplicates and html noise imply candidate preprocessing difference upstream. Are we feeding identical raw candidates?

omar: also check our HTML-stripping microservice version on staging; slight parser diff can change doc text and thus rerank score.

mia: ack will confirm candidate pipeline parity too. initial plan extended: add candidate text checksum comparison between fp32 and int8 runs.

leo: final ask: once you collect artifacts (per-query diffs, histograms, checksums, config), upload to /s3/rerank-triage/6880011222 and link here. we'll decide rollback vs fix after looking.

mia: uploaded artifacts, link: https://s3.company/rerank-triage/6880011222 :ndcg_up_mrr_down_logs

jess: thanks. next steps: if root cause is infra tokenizer or candidate pipeline, fix that. if root cause is quant score compression, we can try calibration (rescale) + re-eval.

sam: prefer short mitigation (rescale) for immediate safety, but pipeline parity fix = long term.

mia: will implement quick rescale experiment (multiplier 1.02) and run A/B on 10k sample overnight. I'll post results tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: "task created: INFRA-2391 ensure quant-runtime deterministic seed flag enabled on staging"

leo: great work everyone. keep notes in the triage doc and ping if you need help analyzing examples.
